effects: Sets ratification[maker][root].isRootRatified to newIsRootRatified. The caller must be the maker or an address the maker authorized on Midnight.
When set to true, every offer in the Merkle tree under that root becomes fillable by takers on Midnight (isRatified passes), so the maker's assets can be traded on those terms.
When set to false, those offers can no longer be taken.
No tokens or native value move, and the function is not payable.
formats.shown: The screen says 'Update order approval' / 'Set order approval of <maker> to Yes/No' and shows the maker, the raw Merkle root and a Yes/No ratified flag.

findings.title: setIsRootRatified: the intent reads like approving the maker address, not enabling a batch of orders to be filled.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json interpolatedIntent 'Set order approval of {#.maker} to {#.newIsRootRatified}'. PriceRatifierV1.sol isRatified: require(ratification[offer.maker][root].isRootRatified, NotRatified()) is what makes every offer in the tree takeable. In case 0 the reader was left unsure 'who gains rights' and 'why the approved party and maker are both my own address'.
findings.fix: Use an intent like 'Enable or disable order batch', with interpolatedIntent 'Allow takers to fill {#.maker}'s orders in this batch: {#.newIsRootRatified}'. Relabel Root as 'Order batch (Merkle root)'.

findings.title: setIsRootRatified: the Merkle root hides the terms of the offers it ratifies.
findings.evidence: PriceRatifierV1.sol isRatified checks HashLib.isLeaf(root, hashPriceRatifierV1Offer(offer, allowedTaker), ...). descriptor.json shows #.root with format 'raw'. Tokens, prices, sizes and allowed takers are not in the calldata.
findings.fix: No descriptor change can decode the tree. A wallet could only check the offers off-chain.

cases.notes: Nothing moved on chain (effects empty). The one effect is ratifying root 0x3b18…a453 for maker 0x958e…1917 (the signer). The reader saw the status change to Yes but did not understand that it lets takers fill the batch's orders.
